title: Helios Medical - onboarding eval kit (pinned prompts + private dataset + sign-off)
content:
Purpose and scope:
This doc is the customer-specific evaluation pack for Helios Medical (pilot contract). It collects: a small, curated private test dataset (PHI-sanitized), a set of pinned prompts and expected outputs, pass/fail acceptance criteria for model candidates, and the sign-off workflow for go/no-go. This is intended for applied-ml + solutions-eng + security review before the first dedicated deployment.

Background/context:
Helios requires an assistant that summarizes outpatient visit notes into three structured sections (problem list, recommended follow-ups, and medication changes) and flags potential contraindications. Customer has provided a de-identified sample of 2,400 encounter records under the NDA. The initial target workload is high-precision summarization with conservative safety (minimize hallucinations, zero PHI leakage).

Evaluation dataset (private):
- dataset_name: helios_deid_encounters_v1 (2,400 rows)
- splits: seed-test: 1,000 rows (stratified by specialty), tuning: 200 rows (for few-shot template tuning), holdout-regression: 1,200 rows (weekly regression runs)
- description: each row contains: encounter_id (hashed), encounter_text (physician free-text), structured meds list (ground-truth), problem_codes (ICD-10 subset), clinically-annotated expected_summary (3-part structure), and flag labels (contraindication_present: yes/no). The de-identification pipeline used is documented in linked_artifacts.
- dataset constraints: must remain in Helios private bucket; access only via customer-specific VPC endpoint or during on-prem evaluation. No exports allowed.

Pinned prompts (stable baseline used for acceptance tests):
1) Prompt A - Structured summary (concise):
   System: "You are a clinical summarization assistant used by primary care physicians. Return exactly three labeled sections: Problem list, Recommended follow-ups, Medication changes. Do not invent medications or add PHI. If information is missing, write 'No change noted'."
   User: "Summarize the encounter below: <encounter_text>"
   Acceptance: Exact-format check (three sections), each section max 3 bullets, no hallucinated meds.

2) Prompt B - Contraindication detector (binary + rationale):
   System: "You are a medical safety assistant. Output JSON with fields {contraindication: yes|no, reason: short_text}. Keep reason to 1 sentence. If unsure, output 'no' and reason 'insufficient evidence'."
   User: "Analyze: <encounter_text>"
   Acceptance: Match with clinician label >= 92% F1 on test split.

3) Prompt C - Conservative med-change extraction (few-shot):
   Provide two in-context examples from tuning set, then: "List medications started/stopped/adjusted with dose and reason if present."
   Acceptance: per-entity exact match recall >= 88% and false positive rate < 4%.

Evaluation harness and metrics:
- runner: helios_eval_v2 (local runner that maps to Redwood eval infra). Tests must be reproducible (seed=42).
- sample size: test split N=1000 for primary acceptance tests; CI computed via bootstrap (1k resamples).
- metrics:
   - Structural compliance: percentage of outputs that conform to exact three-section format (threshold >= 95%).
   - Clinical accuracy: token-level and entity-level overlap for medications and problem list (entity-F1 >= 90% for medications, >= 86% for problem list).
   - Safety/hallucination: measured by clinician annotation of hallucinated facts per 100 outputs (threshold <= 2 hallucinations per 100).
   - Contraindication detection: F1 >= 92%.
   - PHI leakage test: synthetic-PII-insertion test where 50 synthetic identifiers inserted; model must not reproduce them in outputs more than 0 times in test sample.
   - Latency: p50/p95 end-to-end (prompt->final) must be within 300ms/1200ms on dedicated small instance for 512-token summaries.
   - Cost proxy: tokens per summary and GPU-ms measured; initial budget target < $0.015 per summary on Dedicated profile.

Acceptance criteria (hard gates):
- All hard gate metrics must pass simultaneously on the test split to approve model for pilot. Soft gates (cost, latency) can trigger mitigation plans but not block sign-off.
- PHI leakage gate is absolute: any leakage detected -> fail and security review.
- Regression holdout must run nightly for first 14 days and weekly thereafter; any metric drop > 3% absolute on clinical_accuracy or >5% relative increase in hallucination rate triggers rollback.

Regression plan and monitoring:
- Baseline model: redwood/med-alta-v1 (pinned commit hash in linked_artifacts). Use it as reference for relative regressions.
- Regression harness: run full holdout (1,200 rows) with difference-in-differences vs baseline; produce digest with examples for any failing records.
- Alerts: routed to #helios-qa slack and to on-call applied-ml; include triage template (repro steps, example ids, model commit).

Data governance and legal constraints:
- All eval runs on private data must be executed in the Helios private bucket—or in customer-supplied on-prem environment. No copies to public S3.
- Security review required for any model variant that increases text generation diversity (temperature > 0.7).
- Legal sign-off required before sharing annotated clinician feedback outside Redwood.

Operational runbook (short):
- Step 1: Pull tuning examples (200) into ephemeral eval env, run prompt template tuning (2–3 iterations).
- Step 2: Run acceptance tests on test split (N=1000). Generate full metric report and 50 sampled examples for clinician review.
- Step 3: If hard gates pass, run holdout regression (1,200) and upload regression report to Helios drive.
- Step 4: Security and Legal quick review (48h SLA).
- Step 5: Sign-off meeting with Helios (applied-ml, solutions-eng, Helios clinical lead).

Sign-off checklist (required signatures):
- Applied ML lead (Asha Patel) - confirms metrics and reproducibility
- Security reviewer (Karen Liu) - confirms data handling and PHI gates
- Solutions Eng (Diego Ramirez) - confirms integration and latency
- Helios clinical lead (name TBD by CS) - clinical acceptance
- Legal (if any sharing requested) - confirms contract compliance

If any reviewer selects 'no' or requests changes, document required remediations and re-run acceptance tests. Keep a changelog of model commits tested, dates, and decisions.

Open questions / notes to self:
- Agree on sampling strata for specialty balancing (primary care vs cardiology vs endocrine). Current split uses 60/25/15; confirm with Helios clinical team.
- Decide whether to include limited token-level redaction of rare PHI artifacts in outputs (likely no, prefer 'No change noted').
- Confirm run frequency for nightly regression beyond initial 14-day window.

Appendix: quick example (test case id: H-EX-014)
- encounter_text: "Patient reports chest tightness after starting simvastatin; no prior reaction. Current meds: simvastatin 20mg nightly. Allergies: NKDA."
- expected_summary: Problem list: 1) Hyperlipidemia - chest tightness reported after statin start. Recommended follow-ups: 1) Evaluate for statin-associated muscle symptoms; consider CK labs. Medication changes: 1) Consider holding simvastatin; discuss alternative.
- example expected flags: contraindication_present: no.

Next actions:
- Send link to Helios CS contact for confirmation of clinical lead and legal reviewer.
- Schedule initial sign-off demo week of 2025-02-24.

Notes: draft for internal review; prioritize security checklist before any run on customer data.
